title: Locality sees no spacelike scale, and Stein's theorem in GR is a no-local-clock theorem
version: 2026-11-10 note, as committed in this branch
relevance: The note this lane tests: Theorem 1 (local relations are all-or-nothing on spacelike pairs of Minkowski) and Theorem 4 (no nontrivial local clock). A state-defined present is designed to fail their locality assumption.
limits: Internal note, checked only by the session that wrote it (stated on its face); its disconnected-object proofs are flagged there as not fully proven.
locator: Sec. 1 Theorem 1 and corollaries; Sec. 3 Theorem 4; Secs. Limits, Credits
assumptions: Restriction-closed classes of spacetimes containing Minkowski and flat cylinders; local relations preserved and reflected by isometric embeddings with causally convex image.
conclusion: Authors' claims as located: no selective local relation on spacelike pairs; no nontrivial local clock under their criteria; curvature-scalar rules are local on a restricted class.
proof_status: Read, not re-derived by this lane; the note itself flags Theorem 2/4 gaps in the connected category.
open_questions: Does a state-level relation evade Theorem 1 only by abandoning functoriality, i.e. is there a category that still reflects state-level structure?

title: Some results on the mutual information of disjoint regions in higher dimensions
relevance: Q1/Q4 anchor for the massless case: 'I^n(A,B) ~ C_A^n C_B^n (R_A R_B / r^2)^a' for disjoint regions in a d+1-dimensional CFT, a fixed by the vacuum-channel OPE; free massless scalar has 2x = d-1 (capacitance formula). Grounds the power-law, effectively unbounded thickness for massless vacua.
limits: Abstract quoted verbatim (fetched from the arXiv PDF landing text); body not read. The massive-field large-separation regime is outside this paper's stated CFT setting (it treats a small-mass logarithmic correction to the area law), so the exponential-in-separation MI claim for massive fields is NOT supported by this record.

title: Large distance expansion of mutual information for disjoint disks in a free scalar theory

limits: Abstract only; massless/CFT regime per abstract; massive case not read.

title: Entanglement measures and their properties in quantum field theory
relevance: Q1/Q5: for causally disjoint regions there are 'no separable (normal) states ... when the regions touch', a finite 'safety-corridor' is needed, vN entropy is not a good measure, and the authors develop relative entanglement entropy with model-independent bounds; area-law divergences near contact. Grounds the well-definedness constraints on any threshold-defined present.
limits: Abstract read verbatim on the arXiv page (v3, 14 May 2018); chapters not read; whether their measures decay exponentially with separation was not verified.
